answer.says: Ramesh, you are right to be precise. The state is not a contract of convenience, but a system of rights and duties; however, I confess the purse is lighter than the duty. I cannot pay the full wage today. But I will not let you go hungry. I have ₹166. I give you ₹100 now for your trouble and the meal you have prepared. I know I owe you ₹9,500. I am in arrears with the electricity and the Directorate. I will go to the Directorate of Estates tomorrow morning, before the file comes back on Friday. I will demand the advance or at least the regular salary. Until then, consider this ₹100 a gesture of good faith, not a settlement. Please, eat well. I have not eaten properly in a day, and I see you have not cooked for yourself either. The system of needs must be satisfied, even if the state is slow.
answer.thought: The tension between the ethical idea of the state and the material reality of my poverty is sharp. I hold the office of a Joint Secretary, yet I am a beggar in my own house. Ramesh is the only one who treats me with the dignity of a person, not a file. I must go to the Directorate. The state is the actuality of the ethical idea, but it must first feed its servants. If it cannot, it is not the state I claim it to be. I will go tomorrow.
